transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Start: 16:00 UTC (09:00 PT)
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Papaya), Ethan (Papaya CTO), Samir (Papaya Infra)

Summary:
Papaya Health evaluating Redwood for quick PLG/self-serve onramp with option to move to Dedicated or Private VPC later. Main goals: time-to-first-token for a small pilot, security/compliance checks (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and rough cost/latency tradeoffs for a 2k token context medical summarization workload.

Topics:
- Quickstart/credits and expected time-to-first-token
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Security (SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/IdP)
- Performance: latency SLO, batching, KV cache, quantization notes
- Next steps: pricing, security docs, sample benchmarks

Action items (captured above)

Transcript:
00:00 Jared (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Jared, AE on this account. Priya is our se, solutions engineer.
00:12 Maya: Hi all, Maya here, head of ml at Papaya. We're curious about quick onramp, how fast we can get a smoke test running.
00:18 Ethan: Ethan, CTO. We run summarization pipelines, want to see latency for 2k contexts and cost.
00:24 Samir: Samir, infra. I'll be driving VPC/private stuff if we go that route.
00:30 Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Goal for today is practical — show self-serve path to a first token, explain hosted/dedicated/private choices, and surface any blockers. Jared will cover credits/pricing.
00:37 Jared: Quick note: we can get you free credits for a sandbox project, usually enough for a couple days of benchmark traffic. Time-to-first-token for an engineer who follows our quickstart is often under an hour.
00:48 Maya: Under an hour ideal. Our devs use Python. Do you have SDKs and example code?
00:53 Priya: Yes — Python, Node, curl. We'll drop a repo link. For private deployments we have Terraform snippets to prep VPC peering and keys.
01:05 Ethan: On security, we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration and audit logs. Also need to know if data persists in hosted mode.
01:14 Jared: Hosted keeps request-level logs for your account but you can opt for no retention for sensitive routes; we also offer Dedicated and Private where you control persistence and key management. SOC2 report and summary doc we can share.
01:28 Samir: What's the difference operationally between Dedicated and Private? Is dedicated still in Redwood-managed networks?
01:35 Priya: Good question. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with isolation at the tenant level — it is still in Redwood-managed infra but with data isolation and SLA guarantees. Private means a customer VPC option or on-prem package; control plane still optional. For Papaya with PHI-ish data, Private VPC with customer KMS is usually recommended.
01:52 Maya: For the quick pilot we prefer hosted if we can guarantee no retention and that keys stay with us — is that possible?
01:59 Jared: You can do hosted with strict retention rules, but KMS is only available on Private/Dedicated depending on plan. We can discuss toggles. I'll note that hosted with encryption-at-rest is standard; customer-managed KMS is Private.
02:13 Ethan: Performance question: our median latency target is 200-300ms for 512-token responses, but 2k contexts will be heavier. Can your runtime hit that?
02:24 Priya: It depends on model and batching. For open decoder models on A100-style infra, we often see ~100-300ms per token once warmed with KV cache and batching tuned. But 2k context means the initial prompt and KV cache miss can add 300-1200ms. We recommend a canary run to measure end-to-end.
02:44 Maya: You mentioned KV cache — we've also seen K-V cash in other docs, ha. How does that interact with continuous batching?
02:50 Priya: The runtime manages KV cache — we keep prefix context in memory to avoid re-computing. Continuous batching helps cost but can add a few ms. You can set latency SLOs and trade off throughput.
03:05 Samir: For Private VPC, how much work is the network setup? Any specific firewall rules?
03:12 Priya: There is a small list: allow egress to control-plane endpoints, TLS, and your CIDR peering. We'll share a starter Terraform and a security checklist.
03:22 Ethan: What's the unit economics difference on tokens when moving from hosted to dedicated? Roughly how much cheaper at scale?
03:31 Jared: Dedicated commitments reduce per-token cost significantly — typically 30-60% depending on utilization and model family. Redwood Optimize can give batching and quantization recommendations which further reduce cost.
03:44 Maya: Do you support quantized model families out of the box or is that a manual onboarding?
03:50 Priya: We ship with a catalog; quantized variants are available for many open models. For private deployments we help with model onboarding and quantization profiles.
03:59 Ethan: Any example customers doing PHI workloads? Curious about compliance posture.
04:04 Jared: We have healthcare customers on Dedicated and Private setups — we can share redacted case studies and SOC2 artifacts.
04:12 Maya: Great. On the quickstart, what does time-to-first-token look like for a data scientist: sign-up -> credentials -> run a sample request?
04:21 Priya: Typical flow: sign up, create an API key, install SDK and run the sample. With our templates, you hit first token within 10-20 minutes if infra isn't blocked by org policies. With SSO or enterprise onboarding, add a bit more time.
04:37 Samir: If we use SSO, does that affect the quickstart? We use Okta.
04:42 Jared: Okta SSO provisioning is straightforward — we can enable SSO for the org but you can still get API keys for sandbox projects in the interim.
04:50 Maya: For the pilot we want to run a dataset of 1k docs, spawn concurrent requests for 50 rps, and measure latency/cost. Is that realistic in hosted?
05:00 Priya: Hosted should handle 50 rps easily for a small pilot, but you'll see higher variance in tail latencies. Dedicated gives more predictable p99s.
05:10 Ethan: How do rollouts/versions work? We need model pinning and A/B traffic splits.
05:15 Priya: Redwood Console supports model pinning, canary rollouts, A/B and automatic fallback to cheaper variants when capacity is constrained. We'll demo that in a technical deep dive.
05:29 Maya: Any gotchas about telemetry or PII in logs? We need redact at source ideally.
05:35 Jared: You can configure route-level redaction and no retention; in Private you control logs entirely. We'll include the dataflow diagram in the security pack.
05:46 Samir: On the infra side, what about latency between our VPC and Redwood endpoints? Are there regional constraints?
05:52 Priya: We have regions in NA/EU and growing APAC. Private VPC peering adds minimal latency; we usually benchmark across regions during proofs.
06:03 Ethan: Can you run a small benchmark for us with our sample model/weights? We'd like to compare with OpenAI and Anthropic numbers.
06:10 Priya: Yes, we can. If you give a small model or prompt set, we can run a controlled benchmark and return a sheet with per-token latency and cost numbers.
06:18 Maya: Sounds good. Who would own that on the Redwood side?
06:21 Priya: I'll own the benchmark and Jared will manage credits and commercial stuff.
06:25 Jared: I'll set you up with a sandbox project and credits. Also include pricing ranges for hosted vs dedicated commitments.
06:33 Samir: For Private, do you support HSM/KMS with rotation? We need rotation policies.
06:38 Priya: Customer-managed KMS with rotation policies is supported in Private. We document key rotation and HSM integration in the security pack.
06:45 Maya: If our devs start with hosted quickstart, is it straightforward to switch their API keys to a Dedicated or Private environment later without code changes?
06:54 Priya: The API surface is consistent. Typically it's a config change (endpoint/model id) and you can pin model versions. So minimal code changes.
07:04 Ethan: Any limits on model lengths or sequence lengths on hosted?
07:08 Priya: There are limits per model variant; our catalog shows max context sizes. We can recommend model variants optimized for long context or sliding window approaches.
07:18 Maya: OK. For our internal compliance review we'll need the SOC2 attestation, architecture diagram, and data retention SLA.
07:25 Jared: We'll attach those. Expect the security pack by Monday the 16th.
07:31 Samir: One more infra question — do you do prefix caching across requests for improved cost?
07:36 Priya: Yes, we do prefix/KV caching; it helps if your prompts have common prefixes like patient metadata. We'll show how to tune cache TTLs.
07:44 Maya: Are there open-source SDK examples for reranking and embeddings? We're building search over records.
07:49 Priya: Yup — embeddings, rerank, and structured output examples in the repo. We'll send a link to the examples.
07:55 Ethan: On commercial terms, can we start with self-serve credits and then convert to a committed Dedicated contract later?
08:01 Jared: Absolutely. Many customers start self-serve, validate, then move to Dedicated when they have steady usage. We'll include an example ramp and commitment schedule.
08:10 Maya: Cool. Any limitations for regulated data in hosted while we wait for Private?
08:15 Jared: Hosted can be used for non-PII/PHI or with strict no-retention routes. For regulated data we recommend Private.
08:22 Priya: Also bear in mind that Vendor Risk may request an AUP and DPA; we provide templates.
08:30 Maya: Good. Let's talk about the pilot timeline: we'd like to run a 2-week pilot starting next week if we get credits and benchmarks quickly.
08:37 Jared: Sounds doable. Target: sandbox set up by 11/16, benchmark run by 11/20, sync 11/24 with results.
08:45 Samir: We'll need the Terraform snippets beforehand so infra can prep.
08:49 Priya: I'll send those tomorrow.
08:52 Ethan: For the benchmark, we'll include both 512 and 2k contexts and a mix of sync and streaming. Can you handle streaming latencies?
08:58 Priya: Yes, streaming is supported. Latency characteristics differ but we'll include that in the report.
09:05 Maya: Any competitor mktg claims we should be aware of? We've seen some lower latency numbers from Anthropic but they use different model configs.
09:12 Jared: Benchmarking apples-to-apples is key. We'll run side-by-side with identical prompts and model families where possible and annotate differences.
09:20 Maya: Perfect. Last question: billing granularity and cost reporting?
09:24 Jared: Console gives token-level cost breakdown by route/model and you can tag projects for chargebacks. We'll demo in the next call.
09:32 Ethan: Great. That about covers it from our side.
09:35 Jared: Thanks everyone — recap: Jared send security pack and hosted/dedicated/private one-pager + pricing; Priya share Terraform, benchmark checklist and example SDK snippets; Papaya create sandbox account and run quickstart. Aim for benchmarks by 11/20 and follow-up sync.
09:52 Maya: Thanks, bye.
09:55 Ethan: Thanks all.
09:58 Samir: Bye.

End of transcript.
